what_it_does: This paper tackles wireless power transfer for implanted medical devices like pacemakers or neural stimulators. The challenge is delivering power wirelessly through living tissue while keeping the device tiny and safe—avoiding excess heat and strong electromagnetic fields that could harm tissue. The researchers designed a receiver coil just 0.9 cubic centimeters in size that automatically adapts to the electrical properties of the tissue surrounding it, enabling efficient charging without needing a doctor to program it after surgery.
